root_cause.text: The mlx5e driver’s PSP offload object was being unregistered from two teardown paths (`_mlx5e_remove()` and `mlx5e_nic_cleanup()`), causing a double-unregister of the same PSP refcounted resource and a refcount underflow/use-after-free.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description and commit message explicitly state “PSP is unregistered twice in: `_mlx5e_remove -> mlx5e_psp_unregister` and `mlx5e_nic_cleanup -> mlx5e_psp_unregister`,” and the patch removes the direct `mlx5e_psp_unregister(priv);` call from `_mlx5e_remove()`, with the note that “the PSP cleanup happens as part of profile cleanup.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the redundant PSP unregistration from the registered netdev removal path.
intent_record.what: In _mlx5e_remove(), the call to mlx5e_psp_unregister(priv) was deleted from the branch that runs when priv->netdev->reg_state == NETREG_REGISTERED, leaving unregister_netdev(priv->netdev) and _mlx5e_suspend(adev, false) unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the remove path no longer explicitly unregisters PSP before unregistering the net device when the device is already registered. This changes teardown ordering/ownership handling during NIC removal and avoids performing that extra PSP unregistration step in this state.

grouping_result.intent: Remove the redundant PSP unregistration from the registered netdev removal path.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly removes the redundant PSP unregistration from one teardown path, which matches the root cause of double-unregistering the same PSP resource and causing refcount underflow/use-after-free.

candidates.rationale: This is the redundant PSP teardown in the registered netdev removal path. Since the PSP object was also unregistered from mlx5e_nic_cleanup(), calling this here causes a double-unregister of the same refcounted resource, leading to refcount underflow/use-after-free.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the redundant PSP teardown call in _mlx5e_remove(). The vulnerability root cause states that PSP was also unregistered from mlx5e_nic_cleanup(), so this second unregister causes a double-unregister of the same refcounted object, leading to refcount underflow/use-after-free.

In `mlx5e_nic_cleanup()` the code calls `mlx5e_psp_unregister(priv);` unconditionally: `mlx5e_health_destroy_reporters(priv);` followed by `mlx5e_psp_unregister(priv);`. The same commit also adds `mlx5e_psp_cleanup(priv);` in `mlx5e_nic_disable()`, but the shown code does not indicate any guard, refcounting, or single-owner logic preventing repeated unregisters. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present and the fix is not present in this code.
